description: Steady B2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Frantic has /æ/ in its first stressed syllable. Frontier has /ʌ/ or /ɔ/ depending on pronunciation, frenzy has /ɛ/, and frosty has /ɑ/.
Subtle has /ʌ/ in its first syllable. Settle has /ɛ/, saddle has /æ/, and soothe has /uː/.
Reckless has /ɛ/ in its first syllable. Racket has /æ/, rickety has /ɪ/, and rocket has /ɑ/.
Mnemonic begins with /n/ because the initial m is silent. Magnetic begins with /m/, genetic with /dʒ/, and kinetic with /k/.
Xenophobia begins with /z/, the usual sound of initial x in this word. Seniority begins with /s/, phenomenon with /f/, and genocide with /dʒ/.
Psalm begins with /s/ because the p is silent. Palm begins with /p/ in General American, qualm with /kw/, and calm with /k/.
Promptly ends with /tli/. Prompt ends with /t/, prompts with /ts/, and prompter with /tər/.
Twelfth ends with /lfθ/. Twelve ends with /lv/, and twelfths adds a final /s/; twelfthly is not a standard common word.
Risked ends with /t/ because -ed follows the voiceless /k/ sound. Risks ends with /s/, risky with /i/, and risen with /ən/.
Liaison is pronounced /liˈeɪzɑn/. Lesson has /ɛ/, lesion has /iːʒ/, and leisure has /ɛʒ/ in General American.
Supersede is pronounced /ˌsuːpərˈsiːd/. Supervise ends with /aɪz/, superstition with /tʃən/, and superior with /ɪr/.
Occurrence is pronounced /əˈkɜrəns/. Occurred ends with /d/, current has a different stress and ending, and currency ends with /si/.
